credential_full_name.value: Registered Nurse Certified - Inpatient Obstetric Nursing (RNC-OB)

year_launched.note: NCC publishes pass-rate stats starting from 2016 (2,308 candidates), and NCC itself was incorporated in 1975. Year the RNC-OB credential specifically launched is not clearly documented in primary sources.

eligibility.value: Current, active, unencumbered RN licensure in the U.S. or Canada; 24 months of specialty experience as a U.S. or Canadian RN comprised of a minimum of 2,000 hours (lifetime); employment in the specialty within the last 24 months. Both practice time AND hours must be met (not either/or). Specialty experience can include direct patient care, education, administration, or research.

exam_format.value: Computer-based exam delivered at PSI/AMP test centers OR via Live Remote Proctoring (LRP). 175 multiple-choice items (150 scored + 25 unscored pretest). Each question has a stem with three options (one correct, two distractors). 3-hour time limit.

passing_score.value: Criterion-referenced using Rasch / item response theory. No fixed percentage passing level — pass/fail is based on an ability score against a predetermined criterion set by the Content Team. Different exam forms are equated to a common scale.

fee_total.value: $325 USD (includes $50 non-refundable application fee + $275 testing fee). Applies to both Computer Test Center and Live Remote Proctoring formats. Retake = full fee, no discount.

change_request_fee.value: $125 to change exam category, eligibility window, or method (one change allowed)

withdrawal_refund.value: $160 refund of $325 if candidate withdraws per policy (minus any outstanding charges). Bulk-purchase voucher candidates cannot withdraw.

retest_policy.value: 45-day wait period before reapplying after a failed attempt. Maximum of two attempts at the same exam per calendar year. Full fee applies each retake — no discount.

renewal_process.value: Continuing Competency Assessment (CCA) framework. At the start of each 3-year cycle the certificant completes the CCA, which generates a personalized Education Plan listing the specific CE hours required. CE earned AFTER the CCA in the areas defined by the Education Plan counts toward maintenance. A maintenance application + fee must be submitted before the maintenance due date. There is no fixed CE hour count published in the candidate guide — the requirement is individualized by the CCA.

scope_focus.value: Care of the pregnant person after 20 weeks of gestation through discharge, across antepartum, intrapartum, postpartum, and normal newborn areas.

salary_context_rn_median.value: RN median annual wage $93,600 (BLS May 2024 OEWS). Lowest 10% < $66,030; highest 10% > $135,320. BLS does not break out labor-and-delivery RNs separately.

salary_context_ld_estimated.value: Labor and delivery RN average ~$82,500/yr (range $75,100–$103,000) per industry aggregators (Salary.com, Vivian Health) — not BLS-published.

common_confusions.value: RNC-OB is frequently confused with: (1) RNC-MNN (Maternal Newborn Nursing — focuses on level I postpartum/well-newborn rather than full intrapartum continuum); (2) RNC-LRN (Low-Risk Neonatal Nursing); (3) C-EFM (Certified in Electronic Fetal Monitoring — a subspecialty add-on, not a standalone core credential); (4) WHNP-BC (Women's Health Nurse Practitioner — APRN credential, different role); (5) CNM (Certified Nurse-Midwife — different role and certifying body, AMCB).

recent_changes.value: 2026 exam outline is current (as published in the 2026 Candidate Guide). NCC introduced two new subspecialty exams in 2025: Reproductive Health and Infertility (RHI) and Obstetric Emergencies (OBE). The 2025 RNC-OB pass rate dropped sharply to 65% (2,079 candidates) from 86% in 2024 (3,098 candidates) — consistent with a new exam form or revised passing point. NCC also ran a 'Second Chance Free' promotion starting 2025-02-01.

subdomains: Maternal/Birthing Person Complications Affecting the Fetus and Newborn
Maternal/Birthing Person Psychological and Environmental Factors
Recovery and Postpartum Physiology and Complications

competing_credentials.scope: Maternal Newborn Nursing — well-newborn / postpartum focused (level I units)

discrepancies.note: Multiple secondary sources do not consistently report the launch year. NCC pass-rate table starts at 2016 but the credential predates that. Leaving as null per skill rules.

Unlike many specialty credentials with a fixed CE hour count, NCC issues an individualized Education Plan via the CCA. There is no single hour figure in the 2026 candidate guide for RNC-OB. Page copy must say 'CE hours per individualized CCA-generated Education Plan' rather than invent a number.

RNC-OB pass rate dropped from 86% (2024) to 65% (2025) — a 21-point shift. NCC has not publicly explained, but a revised passing point and/or 2026 exam form rollout are likely drivers. Both numbers are pulled directly from NCC's statistics page.
